actions.text: Check drainage first: if water has been standing, the yellowing may be waterlogging, not a lack of fertiliser.
Note which leaves are affected: old lower leaves point to nitrogen/potassium/magnesium; young top leaves point to zinc/iron/sulphur.
Get a soil test (Soil Health Card) to confirm which nutrient is short before adding more.
Top-dress nitrogen (urea) in split doses as per your state recommendation, when the soil is moist; foliar urea spray can give a quick green-up.
Apply sulphur (gypsum or bentonite sulphur) at the recommended rate, especially for oilseeds and pulses.
Take a few affected plants in a paper bag to your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call Kisan Call Centre 1800-180-1551.

text: long grey tan lesions on maize leaves after humid weather

actions.text: Next season, sow a resistant/tolerant variety recommended for your district (ask KVK or seed office).
After harvest, plough in or remove crop residue so the disease does not carry over to the next crop.
Pick off and destroy badly infected leaves or plants away from the field (do not leave them on the bunds).
Spray a fungicide registered for this disease on this crop (e.g. mancozeb, azoxystrobin + difenoconazole) at the first signs, especially before rainy spells. Use the label dose only.

text: caterpillar eating the whorl, sawdust like frass

actions.text: Walk the field in a W pattern and check 20 plants: count how many show the problem before acting.
Install pheromone traps (about 5 per acre) to monitor and mass-trap moths.
Put a pinch of sand or soil-ash mix into the maize whorl to deter fall armyworm larvae.
Put up bird perches (T-shaped sticks, ~10 per acre) so birds eat caterpillars.
Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or a registered biopesticide on young caterpillars.
Spray neem oil / azadirachtin (as per label) on early infestations; repeat after 7-10 days.
If the pest crosses the economic threshold, spray an insecticide registered for this pest on this crop (e.g. emamectin benzoate, chlorantraniliprole, spinetoram). Use the label dose only.
This pest can spread fast across fields: inform your KVK / block agriculture officer so they can warn neighbours.
